caption: Mitral valve, normal and mitral stenosis (columns): LA pressure (black, upstream), LV pressure (grey, downstream; shown only up to 15 mmHg), the transvalvar pressure difference dp (panel -2 to 6 mmHg) and A_eff. Each column digitised every 0.005 s into mynard2012_fig7_mitral_<case>_pressures.csv (P_up = LA, P_down = LV, dp = LA - LV; P_down, dp and u_down are nan while LV is above the 15 mmHg axis top, 0.480 s of the normal and 0.475 s of the stenosis column, i.e. the whole of systole) and mynard2012_fig7_mitral_<case>_A_eff.csv. Time from the 0.2 s scale bar (860.0 px/s); t = 0 at each column's left edge; the columns are 1.024 and 1.027 s wide (beat 0.89 s): each starts in late diastole with the valve open and ends after the next closure. Pressure axes from the ticks 0-15 mmHg, dp -2 to 6, A_eff 0-8 cm2. Where the grey LV line is hidden under LA, LV = LA - dp(panel). normal: LA 5.8-10.7 mmHg, LV down to 5.1 mmHg, closure (A_eff < 0.05 cm2) at 0.100 s and again at 0.995 s, opening at 0.545 s (LA rises above LV at 0.545 s), peak dp 3.66 mmHg at 0.566 s, dp reverses during diastasis (LA below LV from 0.655 to 0.720 s, min -0.23 mmHg), A_eff max 7.69 cm2 (Table III: 1 x A_ann 7.7), partial closure to 3.84 cm2 at 0.850 s; stenosis: LA 6.3-12.1 mmHg, LV down to 4.2 mmHg, closure at 0.105 and 1.000 s, opening at 0.540 s, peak dp 5.33 mmHg at 0.581 s, dp stays positive through diastole (min 1.01 mmHg), A_eff max 2.31 cm2 (M_st 0.3 x 7.7 = 2.31), flat while open. Within a few px of the axis top the steep LV upstroke/downstroke is clipped and left nan.
